title: What Reaction Rate Means
description: Defining reaction rate as change in concentration over time and how it is measured experimentally.
mastery_criteria: Student can express a reaction rate in terms of reactant loss or product gain and state its units.

title: Collision Theory
description: Why reactions require collisions of sufficient energy and correct orientation to occur.
mastery_criteria: Student can explain the two collision requirements and relate collision frequency to rate.

title: Measuring Concentration Over Time
description: Experimental techniques for tracking how reactant and product concentrations change.
mastery_criteria: Student can describe at least two methods for following a reaction's progress and read a concentration-time curve.

title: The Form of a Rate Law
description: How a rate law relates rate to reactant concentrations through a rate constant and orders.
mastery_criteria: Student can write a general rate law and identify the rate constant and reaction orders.

title: Reaction Order & Its Meaning
description: What zero-, first- and second-order dependence tells you about how concentration affects rate.
mastery_criteria: Student can interpret the order with respect to a reactant and the overall reaction order.

title: Finding Order by Initial Rates
description: Using the initial-rates method to determine reaction orders from experimental data.
mastery_criteria: Student can determine reaction orders and the rate constant from a table of initial-rate experiments.

title: Integrated First-Order Rate Law
description: Deriving and using the integrated first-order law, including the linear ln[A] plot.
mastery_criteria: Student can use the integrated first-order equation and recognise its straight-line plot.

title: Integrated Second-Order Rate Law
description: The integrated second-order law and how its 1/[A] plot distinguishes it from first order.
mastery_criteria: Student can apply the integrated second-order equation and identify order from linearised plots.

title: Half-Life & Reaction Order
description: How half-life depends on concentration differently for each reaction order.
mastery_criteria: Student can compute half-life for first-order reactions and explain how it differs by order.

title: Activation Energy & the Energy Barrier
description: The energy barrier a reaction must cross and how it relates to the transition state.
mastery_criteria: Student can define activation energy and sketch a reaction energy profile with a transition state.

title: The Arrhenius Equation
description: How the rate constant depends on temperature and activation energy through the Arrhenius relation.
mastery_criteria: Student can use the Arrhenius equation to find activation energy from rate constants at two temperatures.

title: Reaction Mechanisms & Elementary Steps
description: How an overall reaction is built from elementary steps with their own molecularity.
mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish elementary steps from the overall reaction and state their molecularity.

title: The Rate-Determining Step
description: How the slowest elementary step controls the observed rate law of a mechanism.
mastery_criteria: Student can derive a rate law from a proposed mechanism using the rate-determining step.

title: How Catalysts Work
description: How catalysts provide an alternative pathway with lower activation energy without being consumed.
mastery_criteria: Student can explain how a catalyst changes the energy profile and why it is not consumed.

title: Testing a Mechanism Against Data
description: Checking whether a proposed mechanism is consistent with the experimentally observed rate law.
mastery_criteria: Student can judge whether a mechanism is plausible by comparing its predicted rate law to experiment.
